gap: No result ChatGPT got gives the charging numbers for a D cell. Tenergy rates its 10,000 mAh D at 1,000 mA for 16 hours as a standard charge, 2,000 mA for 7 hours, or 5,000 mA for 2.4 hours with −ΔV cutoff. Its recommended T9688 charger gives D cells only 1,300 mA, so a full 10,000 mAh charge needs at least about 7.7 hours. Tenergy's popular 8-bay TN480U charger takes AA and AAA only and cannot charge D cells at all.
standout_why: I compared against newworldsurvival.com (cited), which says only that 'a universal charger that handles AA, AAA, C, D, and 9V sizes' keeps things simple and gives no current or time figures. I also read reactual.com (cited), which gives no charge current or time and only links to a separate charger post. ChatGPT's second answer already said 'Make sure it explicitly supports D-size NiMH cells.' So the point that you need a D-capable charger is already covered. What's new is the per-slot current, the hours it implies, and the fact that a common Tenergy 8-bay charger cannot take D cells. I did not open popsci, theprepared or commonsensehome.
decides: This confirms the battery picks rather than changing them. It does change what goes with them. A 10,000 mAh D cell needs a charger with D bays, such as the T9688 at 1,300 mA, which Tenergy names for its Centura D, and it still charges overnight, not in an hour or two. The AA/AAA chargers Dealectric already lists (Tenergy TN480U, and TN438 by its listing name) should not be suggested with these batteries. If the shopper wants to power a household of D devices from one charge session, the per-slot current matters more than the 8,000 versus 10,000 mAh label.

findings.label: Rated charge regimes
findings.value: Standard 1,000 mA for 16 h; quick 2,000 mA for 7 h; rapid 5,000 mA for 2.4 h with −ΔV = 5 mV
findings.source_title: Tenergy D 10,000mAh NiMH Rechargeable Battery - Tenergy
findings.note: From the maker's spec block. At the standard rate, 16 h × 1 A = 16 Ah put in for 10 Ah rated, a factor of 1.6.

findings.label: Weight / size / cycles / price
findings.value: 0.36 lb (about 163 g) per cell; 60 mm tall × 32 mm diameter; up to 1,000 recharges; $12.99 per cell
findings.source_title: Tenergy D 10,000mAh NiMH Rechargeable Battery - Tenergy
findings.note: Converted 0.36 lb × 453.6 g/lb ≈ 163 g. This is the flat-top cell; check that the listing is flat-top or button-top before linking it.

findings.label: Maker's charge-time rule and recommended chargers
findings.value: Charge time = 8,000 mAh ÷ charger rate; recommended chargers are Tenergy T9688 and TN299
findings.source_title: Tenergy 16-Pack Centura NiMH D 1.2V 8000mAh Rechargeable Battery
findings.note: Tenergy says to 'take the capacity of the battery (8000mAh) and divide it by the charge rate.' On a T9688 at 1,300 mA that gives 8,000 / 1,300 ≈ 6.2 h, before the charge-efficiency allowance.

findings.label: Self-discharge / cycles / weight / price
findings.value: Retains up to 85% of capacity after 1 year; up to 2,100 cycles; 145 g per cell; 33 × 61 mm; $101.99 per 16-pack
findings.source_title: Tenergy 16-Pack Centura NiMH D 1.2V 8000mAh Rechargeable Battery
findings.note: $101.99 / 16 ≈ $6.37 per cell. The low self-discharge figure is the maker's claim.

findings.label: D-cell charge current and termination
findings.value: 1,300 mA for AA/C/D (500 mA AAA, 30 mA 9V); −ΔV cutoff; 4 independent slots; $40.99
findings.source_title: Tenergy T9688 Universal NiMH/NiCd LCD Battery Charger - Tenergy
findings.note: 10,000 mAh / 1,300 mA ≈ 7.7 h minimum for a 10,000 mAh D. This is less than half of Tenergy's own 2,000 mA quick rate for that cell. The page does not mention a safety timer.

findings.label: Compatible sizes
findings.value: AA and AAA only (8× AA at 500 mA, 8× AAA at 250 mA, 5 V 2 A input); cannot charge C or D; $23.99
findings.source_title: Tenergy TN480U 8-Bay NiMH Battery LCD Display Fast Charger, Micro USB/Type C Input
findings.note: Dealectric already lists this charger (tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger). It is not compatible with any of the D picks.
